extracted.intended_audience: researchers submitting to or reviewing for eLife (authors, reviewers, editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for how eLife conducts peer review and publishes 'Reviewed Preprints', including the two‑dimensional Assessment (significance and strength of evidence) and required content of public reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewed Preprints publication model
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife publishes all peer-reviewed submissions as Reviewed Preprints rather than using traditional accept/reject decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each publication includes the article, peer feedback, author response, and an eLife Assessment. All accepted submissions become preprints; authors may submit revised versions with updated assessments; authors can publish a Version of Record to conclude the review process. Publication fee is $3,000 (waived for those unable to pay). There are no artificial limits on review volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife Assessment — Significance of Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance of Findings — Ranges from "landmark" to "useful". The Assessment summarises the significance of the findings in each article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses a controlled vocabulary: Landmark / Fundamental / Important / Valuable / Useful. The Assessment's significance dimension is intended to communicate how important or field‑changing the reported results are.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife Assessment — Strength of Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Strength of Evidence — Ranges from "exceptional" to "inadequate". The Assessment summarises the strength of evidence in each article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses a controlled vocabulary: Exceptional / Compelling / Convincing / Solid / Incomplete / Inadequate. This dimension reflects the quality, rigor, and sufficiency of the data/analysis supporting the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reviews must describe strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: "Describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public review text should explicitly enumerate what the manuscript does well and where it falls short; this information is visible alongside the article to inform readers and authors. Use concrete examples and link to data/figures where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reviews must indicate whether claims are justified by the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Public reviews should indicate whether "claims and conclusions are justified by the data".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate alignment between data/analyses and the authors' claims, noting any overinterpretation, unsupported inferences, or gaps in evidence. Provide specific counterexamples or required additional analyses if claims are not justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reviews must make explicit disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Public reviews must "make explicit disagreements between reviewers and authors".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where reviewers and authors differ, the review should state the points of disagreement clearly and, where possible, explain the basis (methods, interpretation, or data). This transparency should include any unresolved disputes reflected in the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors — all active researchers — select submissions for peer review based on criteria detailed in eLife's article 'How and why eLife selects papers for peer review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial triage/selection is performed by active‑researcher editors using selection criteria described elsewhere; authors should consult that guidance to understand thresholds for being sent for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative assessment preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers consult during assessment writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment text is produced following consultation between editors and reviewers to ensure the Assessment summarises the consensus (or notes dissent) about significance and evidence strength. This is a procedural standard intended to improve accuracy and fairness of the Assessment.
